text:
morgan: paging oncall — seeing a GPU OOM cascade on streaming-decode cluster, containers restarting repeatedly, requests dropping. hitting customers in eu-west1. raising incident. @oncall-bot please page.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT/PAGE triggered for severity=high, service=streaming-decode, region=eu-west1. Pager sent to: @sanjay (oncall).
sanjay: acked. joining. any quick signal on whether this is runaway generation or config mismatch?
morgan: early signal looks like runaway sequences beyond max_tokens, but logs show containers fail before the stream finishes. sample trace: `cudaErrorIllegalAddress -> invalid device pointer -> process crash -> container restart`.
devin: pulling logs now. grep output: ```
2026-11-03T04:32:10Z decode[pid=4212]: decode: started seq id=xyz
2026-11-03T04:33:02Z decode[pid=4212]: cuda: cuCtxSynchronize() failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
2026-11-03T04:33:02Z kernel: oom-killer invoked for process decode[4212]
2026-11-03T04:33:03Z containerd: restart backoff for decode-abc (restart_count=3)
```
devin: also seeing a pattern where the request.max_tokens header is missing for some SDK clients, so the runtime falls back to default unbounded token cap for certain routes.
elaine: datadog chart — GPU memory usage spikes in 2 nodes, then container crash, then traffic migrates and triggers the next node (cascade).
sanjay: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) push a temporary routing rule to drop requests above a conservative token limit for streaming endpoints, 2) enable smaller fallback model for streaming, 3) cordon affected nodes and scale up decode pool. thoughts?
morgan: concur. also we should add a short-lived proxy filter to enforce `X-Max-Tokens` default of 512 when header absent.
devin: I can flip a config in the edge proxy in 2 mins: `/svc/proxy/filters/force_max_tokens` set to 512 and enable for streaming routes. will deploy via canary 5%.
sanjay: do canary immediately. tag rollout with `oom-mitigation-323999` and watch errors.
opsbot: deploy started: service=proxy, env=prod, canary=5%, tag=oom-mitigation-323999. CI job #48721.
morgan: also open fallback path: route ~20% of streaming traffic to `gpt-small-quant` model variant with lower mem. set routing policy `pref_fallback_model=gpt-small-quant` for eu-west1.
devin: routing change pushed. `kubectl apply -f /deploy/routing/oom-fallback-eu-west1.yaml` (applied).
elaine: metrics 90s after canary: GPU memory usage per-node down ~30% on canaried nodes, request drops reduced but still ~8% drop rate across region.
sanjay: next step: label/cordon the two nodes that crashed to prevent scheduling until investigation. `kubectl cordon node-az3-decode-07` and `node-az3-decode-09`.
devin: cordoned. also increased replica count by +4 in decode pool — `kubectl scale deployment/decode-pool --replicas=18`.
oncall-bot: Handoff reminder in 30m.
morgan: customer impact: initial spike affected ~4 customers with heavy streaming usage. CS ticket created: CS-9182. they reported partial transcript truncation and retries. estimated affected requests: ~12% of streaming requests in eu-west1 between 04:30-04:40 UTC.
cust-success: customer note — sending proactive comms to Customer A and B, asking for request IDs for correlation.
sanjay: root cause hypothesis: misapplied token-cap defaults + a set of SDK clients that omit max_tokens header -> unbounded loops -> KV cache growth + decoder memory pressure -> illegal memory access -> process crash. The cascade is caused by traffic failover scheduling onto remaining nodes.
morgan: mitigation status: proxy filter canary=done, fallback model routing applied, damaged nodes cordoned, decode pool scaled. observed drops down to ~1.5% now.
devin: logs show fewer `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` after fallback applied. still a residual OOM in one older GPU instance type `g2-legacy-04` — scheduling rule may still place some heavy requests there.
sanjay: add a temporary nodeSelector to avoid `g2-legacy-04` until repro and fix. `kubectl patch deployment decode-pool -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"gpu-type":"no-legacy"}}}}}'`.
elaine: monitoring note: set an alert to fire if per-node GPU mem deltas exceed 85% for >30s. created alert id: ALERT-STREAM-3239.
opsbot: alert created ALERT-STREAM-3239 for condition gpu.mem_pct > 85% for 30s.
morgan: customer impact summary for post-incident: 4 enterprise customers saw partial failures, some retried and succeeded, a couple had truncated responses. CS is drafting an RCA notice.
sanjay: who will own the postmortem? I can own investigation & fixes for routing and defaults. devin will own runtime crash analysis. morgan will own customer comms.
devin: owning runtime. initial reproducer: running long generation with `max_tokens=unbounded` on latest decoder binary causes KV cache to grow and on `g2-legacy-04` memory allocator trips, causing illegal pointer access. reproducer script in gist: `https://gist.github.com/devin/repro-oom-323999`.
morgan: tickets: infra-4527 (cordon & node quarantine), runtime-9983 (debug allocator & crash dump), proxy-7721 (force max_tokens filter) assigned to devs.
sanjay: 1 hour timeline: will keep the incident open until all nodes back to normal and postmortem started. If drops <1% for 30m, we can move to mitigated.
oncall-bot: Reminder: 30m to next handoff.
elaine: metrics trending: after 25m stabilization, request drop rate stabilized at 0.9% and GPU mem usage stable.
morgan: recording final mitigation actions: - force_max_tokens proxy filter (512) enabled globally for streaming - routing fallback to `gpt-small-quant` in eu-west1 - cordoned nodes: node-az3-decode-07, node-az3-decode-09 - added nodeSelector to avoid `g2-legacy-04` - scaled decode pool +4 - ALERT-STREAM-3239 created - CS ticket CS-9182 created.
sanjay: closing note: schedule follow-up postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC. link to incident board: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-323999. assign owners as noted.
opsbot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated. duration 00:52:49.
morgan: thanks all. handing off to next oncall for follow-up. please paste crash dumps & repro logs in runtime-9983.
sanjay: ack handoff. I'll take over for follow-ups.
